sentence: Pregabalin is a prescription medicine used for nerve pain, epilepsy and generalised anxiety disorder.
note: NHS About pregabalin and MedlinePlus summaries: used for neuropathic pain, epilepsy, generalised anxiety disorder; nerve pain is pain from damaged nerves.

sentence: It most often causes sleepiness, dizziness and headaches.
note: NHS: most common are sleepy, dizzy, headaches; usually mild, go away by themselves.

sentence: Some people can become addicted to it, and in the UK it is a controlled medicine.
note: NHS summary: some people can become addicted.

sentence: For epilepsy, pregabalin is thought to reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
note: NHS summary: epilepsy abnormal electrical activity; nerve pain blocks messages; anxiety stops release of chemicals.

sentence: For nerve pain, it is thought to block pain by interfering with pain messages travelling through the brain and down the spine.
note: NHS summary: epilepsy abnormal electrical activity; nerve pain blocks messages; anxiety stops release of chemicals.

sentence: For anxiety, it is thought to stop the brain from releasing the chemicals that make a person feel anxious.
note: NHS summary: epilepsy abnormal electrical activity; nerve pain blocks messages; anxiety stops release of chemicals.

sentence: MedlinePlus places pregabalin in a group of medicines called anticonvulsants.
note: MedlinePlus summary: anticonvulsant; neuropathic pain in diabetes and post-shingles; avoid alcohol as it adds to drowsiness.

sentence: The NHS says it takes at least a few weeks for pregabalin to work.
note: NHS: takes at least a few weeks.

sentence: The NHS says the most common side effects are feeling sleepy, feeling dizzy and headaches.
note: NHS: most common are sleepy, dizzy, headaches; usually mild, go away by themselves.

sentence: The NHS says these side effects are usually mild and go away by themselves.
note: NHS: most common are sleepy, dizzy, headaches; usually mild, go away by themselves.

sentence: NHS trust leaflets list vision disturbances, indigestion, weight gain, leg swelling, tremor and tiredness as other possible effects.
note: Dudley NHS leaflet / South Tees leaflet summaries list vision disturbances, indigestion, weight gain, leg swelling; tremor and tiredness common.

sentence: The NHS describes a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) as rare, and lists swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or fast or struggling breathing, as signs to call 999.
note: NHS side effects summary: lips/mouth/throat swelling or struggling breathing = call 999; hallucinations = call a doctor or 111 now; A&E after taking more than prescribed with sleepiness, confusion, agitation, seizure, passing out.

sentence: The NHS lists hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there) as a reason to call a doctor or NHS 111 now.
note: NHS side effects summary: lips/mouth/throat swelling or struggling breathing = call 999; hallucinations = call a doctor or 111 now; A&E after taking more than prescribed with sleepiness, confusion, agitation, seizure, passing out.

sentence: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust notes that a few people taking pregabalin have had suicidal thoughts, which can happen after only a week of treatment.
note: Guys and St Thomas page: a few people taking pregabalin have had suicidal thoughts, possible after only a week.

sentence: For thoughts of harming oneself or ending one's life, the NHS lists 999 or A&E; NHS 111 (mental health option) and Samaritans on 116 123, which is free at any time, can also help.
note: NHS side effects summary lists thoughts of self-harm under 999/A&E. Samaritans 116 123 and NHS 111 mental health option are standard signposting (textbook).

sentence: The NHS says to go to A&E now after taking more than the prescribed amount if there is sleepiness, confusion, agitation, a seizure or fainting.
note: NHS side effects summary: lips/mouth/throat swelling or struggling breathing = call 999; hallucinations = call a doctor or 111 now; A&E after taking more than prescribed with sleepiness, confusion, agitation, seizure, passing out.

sentence: The MHRA says pregabalin has been linked to infrequent reports of severe breathing difficulty (respiratory depression), including some cases in people not taking opioids.
note: MHRA Feb 2021 DSU: infrequent reports of severe respiratory depression, some without opioids; higher risk: compromised respiratory function, respiratory/neurological disease, renal impairment, CNS depressants, older people.

sentence: The MHRA says gabapentin and pregabalin can cause potentially fatal respiratory depression, particularly when used with opioid medicines and alcohol.
note: MHRA DSU summary: CNS depression resulting in drowsiness, sedation and potentially fatal respiratory depression, particularly with opioids and alcohol.

sentence: The NHS says some people can become addicted to pregabalin, and that the dose is reduced gradually when stopping to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
note: NHS summary: reduce gradually to avoid withdrawal; do not stop without talking to doctor.

sentence: The NHS says not to stop pregabalin without talking to the doctor.
note: NHS summary: reduce gradually to avoid withdrawal; do not stop without talking to doctor.

sentence: The NHS lists groups who may not be able to take pregabalin, including people who have had an allergic reaction to it, who have ever misused or been addicted to a medicine, or who have breathing problems, heart disease, or liver or kidney disease.
note: NHS summary lists allergy, misuse/addiction, breathing, heart, liver, kidney.

sentence: The NHS says pregabalin in pregnancy is usually only advised if a doctor thinks the benefits outweigh the possible risks, and suggests talking to a doctor or pharmacist before breastfeeding.
note: NHS summary: pregnancy usually only advised if benefits outweigh risks; breastfeeding talk to doctor/pharmacist.

sentence: Some brands of pregabalin liquid may contain sodium, so people on a controlled-sodium diet are advised to check first.
